items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of the view that Polymorphism is the most important feature of object-oriented programming.
items.answer: Polymorphism is central to flexible OOP design, but its value relies on the other features; "most important" depends on the problem.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: enables extensible, loosely coupled code; supports design patterns and frameworks. Arguments against: depends on inheritance/interfaces and encapsulation to be useful; can make control flow harder to trace; encapsulation arguably delivers more everyday benefit. Supported judgement: Polymorphism is central to flexible OOP design, but its value relies on the other features; "most important" depends on the problem.

items.stem: To what extent is it true that Programmers should always design to interfaces rather than concrete classes?
items.answer: Programming to interfaces is valuable at module boundaries and where variation is expected; it should not be applied mechanically everywhere.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: loose coupling – implementations can be swapped (e.g. for testing); supports polymorphism and multiple types. Arguments against: extra layers add complexity to small programs; premature abstraction can make code harder to follow. Supported judgement: Programming to interfaces is valuable at module boundaries and where variation is expected; it should not be applied mechanically everywhere.
